articles.title: Millonarios 2027: la lista de refuerzos y las posiciones que buscará Alberto Gamero
articles.standfirst: El Embajador trabaja en el equipo del próximo año con varios puestos en la mira
articles.summary: El Embajador trabaja en el equipo del próximo año con varios puestos en la mira
articles.body: Aunque Millonarios se encuentra enfocado de lleno en los retos definitivos de la presente temporada, en los escritorios de la institución azul ya se trabaja con la mirada puesta en el futuro. La dirección deportiva y el cuerpo técnico encabezado por Alberto Gamero han comenzado a trazar la hoja de ruta para el armado del plantel de cara a 2027, con la firme intención de sumar jerarquía, equilibrio y variantes en posiciones estratégicas. De acuerdo con la información revelada por el periodista Guillermo Arango en La FM, la dirigencia de Millonarios tiene mapeadas tres zonas específicas del campo que considera urgentes de potenciar de cara al próximo año: La planificación de las nuevas caras para 2027 también coincide con un momento de decisiones administrativas complejas con varios elementos de peso en la plantilla actual, cuyos contratos expiran a finales de año. Figuras de peso y referentes del club como el capitán David Mackalister Silva, junto a nombres importantes como Sergio Mosquera, Danovis Banguero, Leonai Souza, Carlos Darwin Quintero, Julián Angulo, Rodrigo Contreras y Stiven Vega, se encuentran bajo la lupa de la gerencia deportiva para definir quiénes continuarán en el proyecto y qué bajas se oficializarán en el corto plazo. La expectativa entre la hinchada empieza a crecer ante los primeros movimientos del mercado de fichajes. El objetivo de la directiva es claro: blindar el proyecto deportivo con las piezas necesarias para que Alberto Gamero cuente con una nómina competitiva que responda a la alta exigencia de la hinchada tanto en el rentado nacional como en los escenarios internacionales.

articles.title: Dietmar Hamann asegura que Luis Díaz está fuera de forma en el Bayern
articles.standfirst: El ex del Bayern lanza dura crítica con el estado actual de Luis Díaz, quien solo ha podido hacer dos goles en la presente campaña
articles.summary: El ex del Bayern lanza dura crítica con el estado actual de Luis Díaz, quien solo ha podido hacer dos goles en la presente campaña
articles.body: El rendimiento del extremo colombiano Luis Díaz en el Bayern Múnich vuelve a estar en el centro del debate europeo. Las críticas más recientes han llegado de una voz más que autorizada en el entorno del gigante alemán, el exjugador Didi Hamann, quien analizó el presente del atacante y aseguró sin rodeos que el ‘cafetero’ se encuentra actualmente fuera de su nivel óptimo de forma. Tras deslumbrar en su primera etapa con el conjunto bávaro —donde registró cifras de absoluto destaque con 26 goles y 23 asistencias en 51 partidos—, el panorama actual de Díaz en la temporada 2026-2027 dista mucho de aquel brillo inicial. En lo que va del curso, el extremo colombiano ha disputado nueve encuentros oficiales en los que apenas ha podido inflar las redes en dos ocasiones y no registra asistencias. A esto se le suma una cuota considerable de mala fortuna y precisión milimétrica, con varios goles anulados por fuera de lugar que han cortado su ritmo ofensivo. Para Hamann, la merma en el impacto del colombiano sobre el terreno de juego es evidente, señalando que "está fuera de forma" y al equipo le cuesta encontrar variantes determinantes en el uno contra uno por la banda cuando el extremo no logra pesar en los metros finales. "El Bayern se está volviendo demasiado dependiente de Olise. Si él no hace nada, ¡nadie más lo hará! Es un jugador excepcional. Ni siquiera quiero imaginar qué pasará sin Olise si está de baja durante un periodo prolongado", señala Hamann. A pesar de los cuestionamientos externos de figuras históricas como Hamann, la interna del Bayern Múnich mantiene la calma y el respaldo hacia el extremo de la Selección Colombia. Directivos y cuerpo técnico han apuntado a que el jugador mantiene una actitud participativa en los circuitos de juego y confían en que recuperará su versión más desequilibrante a medida que avance el calendario europeo. El propio futbolista ha tenido que lidiar con cargas físicas exigentes, lo que incluso lo llevó a ausentarse de algunas convocatorias recientes con el combinado nacional para gestionar los esfuerzos de la temporada. El reto para Luis Díaz pasa ahora por revertir las valoraciones de la crítica alemana, recuperar la finura de cara al arco rival y consolidarse de nuevo como el socio ideal en el ataque del cuadro bávaro.

images.caption: La dura crítica que sacude al Bayern Múnich por Luis Díaz.

articles.title: Missouri vs Ole Miss Prediction: Odds, expert picks, team and player news, betting trends, and stats
articles.summary: Missouri Tigers vs Ole Miss Rebels Game Preview
articles.body:
One of three ranked SEC matchups this weekend is #13 Missouri (5-1) headed to Oxford, MS for a battle with the #9 Ole Miss Rebels (4-1). Ole Miss routed Vanderbilt 52-17 last week following the bye week and couldn't have looked more crisp. Missouri on the other hand smoldered Texas A&M 27-6 and ran for more yards (247) than the Aggies had as an offense (216). Missouri is 7-1 all-time against Ole Miss as the last meeting was in 2019. Ole Miss' lone win in the series came in 1974, 10-0!

We can surely expect more than 10 points in this game as both offenses looked good last week. Missouri has ran for 467 yards and five touchdowns over the last two weeks with Jamal Roberts totaling 433 of those yards and all five scores. Ahmad Hardy has not returned to practice, so it's been an opportunistic year for Roberts.

This game is also a headliner quarterback Austin Simmons following his transfer from Ole Miss. Simmons has been fantastic for Missouri. He has a 14:1 TD to INT ratio after tossing his first pick of the season last week, plus a 64.8 completion percentage and 1,474 yards. Simmons was injured at Ole Miss and never saw the field as a starter for the Rebels again. Simmons was replaced by Trinidad Chambliss and we all know how that turned out.

If the season ended today, Ole Miss would more than likely be in the college football playoff. The Rebels outgained Vanderbilt in yards last week 409-343 and forced four turnovers. The Rebels defense had its best showing against a P4 opponent holding the Commodores to 2.8 yards per carry, four punts, and two turnover on downs.

The offense received a boost with Kewan Lacy returning to the lineup. Lacy ran for 39 yards and a touchdown on seven carries in the first half as Pete Golding eased him back into action. The Rebels ran for 196 yards and three scores, while Trinidad Chambliss accounted for one of those on top of airing it out for three touchdowns and 213 yards. Ole Miss looked like a contender out of the bye week, but Missouri is a step up in completion and playing well with their 1-2 punch of Simmons and Roberts.

Let's dive into the schools on both sides of the ball, look at a few key players, and see where the numbers take us.

Game Details and How to Watch Missouri vs Ole Miss

The latest odds as of Friday courtesy of DraftKings :

Moneyline: Missouri Tigers (+185), Ole Miss Rebels (-225)

Head Coach: Eli Drinkwitz 2026 Record: 5-1 (2-1) Offensive Points Per Game: 35.8 (33rd) Defensive Points Per Game: 16.6 (25th) 2026 Strength of Schedule: 43rd 2026 Remaining Strength of Schedule: 2nd

Missouri ran impressive in the win over Texas A&M. The Tigers ran for 247 rushing yards and the Aggies had 216 as a team. Missouri posted 394 yards of offense and had 20 first downs to Texas A&M's 10. Missouri scored on five out of 10 drives starting from the second quarter and Jamal Roberts had back-to-back 200-yard rushing performances. Roberts is the hottest running back in the country right now with 211 and 222 rushing yards against Florida and Texas A&M, along with five touchdowns. Roberts has four games of 100-plus yards this season and scored in five out of six games.

Missouri Player to Watch on Offense: QB Austin Simmons

Austin Simmons is set for a revenge game against Ole Miss and the guy who replaced him; Trinidad Chambliss . This will be fun! Simmons has looked great for Missouri and threw a season-high 340 yards against Florida two weeks ago. Simmons has four multi-touchdown games and tossed three scores against Kansas and Mississippi State. He wasn't asked to air it out early in the season, but over the past three games he's averaged 32.3 pass attempts per game compared to 22.6 in the first three weeks. If Jamal Roberts can't find running lanes, then Simmons will surely be dropping back 30-plus times and looking to take matters into his own hands late. Simmons has 11 rushing attempts on the season and hasn't scored a touchdown on the ground yet. He's a sneaky anytime touchdown bet.

Versus a DI opponent, Missouri allowed a season-low in yards last week to Texas A&M at 216. Only 27 of those yards came on the ground as the Aggies were held to 1.2 yards per carry and no touchdowns. Missouri picked off Marcel Reed twice and held him to 19-of-39 (48.7%). Missouri ranks tied for 13th nationally with 3.0 sacks per game and ranks tied for 9th with 18 sacks on the season. The Tigers grabbed three sacks last week are they're coming into the week at 31.2% on third downs (26th). Missouri held Texas A&M to 4-of-18 last week on third downs (22.2%). Missouri will be bringing the pressure, but Chambliss thrives under duress. It should be a fun to watch the chess match between Missouri's edge rushers and Chambliss.

Missouri Player to Watch on Defense: EDGE Deaden Hopkins

Deaden Hopkins has only played in four out of Missouri's six games, but boy has he made his presence felt. Hopkins has at least a 0.5 sack in all four games, including Texas A&M last week. Hopkins had a career-high 3.5 sacks at Mississippi State after posting 1.5 sacks versus both Troy and Kansas, plus a forced fumble and recovery in both too. If you catch yourself going "who was that" or "that was close to being offsides"; it's probably Hopkins off the ball you're talking about.

Ole Miss came out the bye week swinging! The Rebels scored 52 at Vanderbilt and 409 yards of offense. Ole Miss ran for 196 yards and Kewan Lacy made his return in limited fashion. Three different players ran for a touchdown, including Trinidad Chambliss . The star quarterback tossed three touchdowns and 213 yards on 20-of-30 (66.6%), plus the rushing score. The Rebels average 300.6 passing yards per game (15th), but 104th in rushing yards per game (133.2). Luckily, Missouri's weak spot is their secondary as they rank 71st in coverage grades as to the 21st rush grade on defense.

Ole Miss Player to Watch on Offense: RB Kewan Lacy

Kewan Lacy only had seven carries in his return following the bye week, but had an efficient 39 yards and a two-yard touchdown. Lacy broke off a 19-yarder in the first quarter and that was the only other highlight as he didn't receive a carry in the second half. Pete Golding say he wanted to slowly bring back Lacy last week, but with a ranked matchup versus Missouri, we can expect at least double-digit touches for Lacy this weekend.

The Ole Miss defense forced four turnovers at Vanderbilt on two interceptions and two fumbles. The Rebels grabbed a pair of turnover in each half and held Vanderbilt to a punt, turnover, or turnover on downs on nine out of 12 drives minus a kneel down. It was the best defensive outing of the year against a P4 opponent. Ole Miss grabbed three sacks and eight TFL, plus forced three fumbles. Missouri has had a lot of success on the ground in the last two games and Ole Miss allowed 2.8 yards per carry to Vanderbilt as the Rebels rank 59th in rush defense grade per PFF.

Ole Miss Player to Watch on Defense: DE Blake Purchase

Blake Purchase is coming off a season-high 2.0 sacks at Vanderbilt to take the team lead of 3.5. Purchase has a sack in three out of five games (Louisville, LSU, Vanderbilt) and forced his first fumble of the year against the Commodores. Purchase is at 6.5 TFL and is a game or two away from surpassing his career high of 34 tackles with Oregon last season.

Vaughn Dalzell (@VmoneySports) leans Ole Miss to cover:

"Missouri historically under Eli Drinkwitz hasn't performed versus ranked opponents or as a road underdog. Missouri is 9-20 on the ML and 13-15-1 ATS against ranked opponents and 2-17 on the ML as a road underdog (7-12 ATS). Ole Miss' offense looked crisp out of the bye week at Vanderbilt; and that's without Kewan Lacy at 100-percent. If Ole Miss can slow down Jamal Roberts just a bit, then the Rebels should cover the -5.5. I doubt Missouri wants Austin Simmons in a shootout with Trinidad Chambliss as much as Simmons wants that."

articles.title: Welsh Cup: TNS among five Cymru Prem sides into third round
articles.summary: The New Saints survive a late scare to beat Airbus Broughton UK 2-1 and advance to the 2026/27 Welsh Cup third round.
articles.body:
The New Saints survived a late scare to beat Airbus Broughton UK 2-1 in the first all-Cymru Premier tie of the season and advance to the 2026/27 Welsh Cup third round.

Dan Williams scored late to ensure the current Cymru Premier leaders were not dealt an upset defeat after Jordan Evans cancelled out Dan Davies' early strike.

TNS were knocked out in the third round by Cardiff Met last season, and could draw the Students again after their 4-0 triumph over Ynyshir Albions.

Fellow top-flight sides Connah's Quay Nomads, Cambrian United and Briton Ferry Llansawel are also in the hat for the third round.

Connah's Quay, two-time winners of the competition, beat Porthmadog 4-0 while Cambrian United beat Trethomas Bluebirds 5-0, with Dylan Edwards scoring twice.

Briton Ferry Llansawel cruised past Afan United with Luke Bowen scoring a 16-minute hat-trick, and goals from Joseph Lloyd and Corey Hurford in a 5-0 win.

Bowen was not the only man to score a second-round hat-trick as Tim Parker fired three for Caerau Ely in their 6-0 dismantling of Cymru South strugglers Llanelli Twn.

Swansea-based Rockspur Fords edged a seven-goal thriller against Evans & Williams, winning 4-3 thanks to a decisive fourth goal from Daniel Williams.

Bangor City 1876 are also through to the third round after beating Cymru North rivals Denbigh Town 2-0.

Further second-round ties are set to take place on Saturday and Sunday.

articles.title: Atlético Madrid have already made a call on on-loan Jonathan David’s future
articles.summary: The brass at La Liga giants Atlético Madrid have already seen enough to make a definitive call on the long-term future of Jonathan David with the club.This c...
articles.body:
The brass at La Liga giants Atlético Madrid have already seen enough to make a definitive call on the long-term future of Jonathan David with the club.

This comes amid the understanding that the Rojiblancos are ready to do whatever it takes to make the Canadian international's signing a permanent one.

Frontman David of course swapped Italy for Spain this past summer. Out of favour at Serie A heavyweights Juventus, the 26-year-old was snapped up by Atlético on a loan deal through next summer.

David has since gone on to impress in the colours of his new employers, to the tune of five direct goal contributions in four La Liga appearances.

And as alluded to above, if the latest word stemming from the Spanish media is anything to go by, such production has already proven enough to convince those behind the scenes at the Metropolitano of the attacker's place in the club's long-term vision.

'The club are already exploring options to secure the striker's services permanently. All indications are that if an agreement isn't reached on the payment method or amount, Atlético are prepared to pay the full fee (€25 million). Furthermore, a portion of next season's budget has already been set aside for this transfer.'

articles.title: Lakers vs. Nuggets: What to watch in preseason finale
articles.summary: The Lakers close preseason against the Nuggets with two starting spots unsettled, availability questions and rebounding issues to address.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers have one more preseason game to work through their questions before the results begin to count.

Friday's finale against the Denver Nuggets offers another opportunity to evaluate the two open starting spots, address rebounding concerns and potentially get several players back on the floor.

Practice brought encouraging updates this week, but availability will determine how much JJ Redick can learn from his final preseason look.

So here are three things to watch for as we FINALLY end the preseason.

Will the Lakers get a more complete look?

Luka Dončić was a full participant in Thursday's practice after sitting out Tuesday's game in Las Vegas. If he plays Friday, watch how the offense operates with Dončić, Austin Reaves and Walker Kessler finally all on the floor together.

Kessler's screening and movement toward the basket should give both guards another option, while their ability to draw defenders can create opportunities for him around the rim. Getting those reads and chemistry right requires possessions together.

Collin Sexton went without the kinesiology tape on his right leg at Friday's shootaround after wearing it Thursday. Maybe we see him make his Lakers debut on Friday.

Ziaire Williams also practiced fully Thursday, saying the swelling in his left foot had subsided and he "felt great." His potential return would give Redick another wing to evaluate alongside the main group.

Adou Thiero was limited Thursday for what Redick described as "just maintenance." Cameron Carr did not practice, and the Lakers had not disclosed why he was unavailable in Las Vegas or Thursday, though he remained with the team.

Any final clues about the starting lineup?

The two starting spots alongside Dončić, Reaves and Kessler remain a storyline entering the finale.

Even Quentin Grimes, who has started every preseason game, offered no answers when asked whether anyone on the team knew who would fill them.

"I don't know. I guess you're going to find out next Wednesday," Grimes said.

He described the process as creating "healthy competition" throughout camp. Friday provides one more opportunity for players to make their case.

Watch which combinations Redick uses with his three established starters, particularly if more wings are available. The opening lineup will draw attention, but the substitutions could offer just as much insight into which players fit together.

Spacing, defensive assignments and the ability to contribute without needing the ball should all matter in those decisions.

The Lakers have been outrebounded in three of their four preseason games while allowing an average of 14.8 offensive rebounds in those games. The most was 20 against the Kings last Thursday.

This prompted Redick to devote practice time to the issue. L.A. went through "three different box-out drills" Thursday.

Friday offers a chance to see whether that work produces better habits.

Watch what happens when a shot goes up: whether defenders find a body, whether guards help collect rebounds and whether the Lakers finish possessions after forcing misses.

Kessler can help protect the basket, but securing the rebound requires everyone to stay involved. That is one area where the Lakers can show progress regardless of who is available.

articles.title: Alamo Heights quarterback Easton Stone voted Express-News Athlete of the Week
articles.summary: The senior threw for 276 yards and four touchdowns on 15-of-21 passing in a 63-31 victory over fellow Class 5A power Liberty Hill.
articles.body:
With Alamo Heights looking to stay in the hunt for a District 13-5A-II title and facing a showdown with another Class 5A power, Liberty Hill, quarterback Easton Stone answered the call.

The senior led the Mules' potent offense to perfection in a 63-31 victory over the Panthers, and now he has been voted Express-News Athlete of the Week.

Stone completed 15 of 21 passes for 276 yards and four touchdowns against Liberty Hill, continuing a strong senior campaign. The win moved Alamo Heights (6-1, 2-1) into a tie for second with Liberty Hill and Liberty Hill Legacy Ranch, just one loss behind undefeated Boerne. The Mules lost a heartbreaker to the Greyhounds, 38-31, in the district opener.

Stone beat out four fellow finalists in the Athlete of the Week poll.

Devine junior Enoch Hall was the engine for the Warhorses against Poteet, averaging 14.5 yards per carry. He finished with 160 rushing yards and five touchdowns in the 47-6 win over the Aggies, earning Offensive Player of the Week honors.

The Defensive Player of the Week, Brandeis junior Ah'maury Hamilton, recorded a team-high 19 tackles in a vital 33-29 win over Churchill. The victory was the Broncos' first 28-6A win of the season and helped them stay in the playoff picture.

Alamo Heights sophomore Mia Moshier was named Volleyball Player of the Week after she combined for 41 kills in a pair of wins over McCollum and Jay. She stuffed the stat sheet against the Cowboys, notching 25 kills, 19 digs and four blocks in a four-set victory.

San Antonio Christian junior Sara Cleveland combined for 44 kills, 11 blocks and 31 digs across three matches as the Lions beat Laredo St. Augustine, St. Anthony and Brownsville St. Joseph. She notched her 1,000th career kill against St. Joseph.

articles.title: Five Key Visits to Track Out West This Weekend
articles.summary: We track the five most significant visits being taken by Western recruits this weekend...
articles.body:
There are several key games taking place this weekend, with Big Ten, Big 12 and SEC schools hosting key games.

But here, we track the five most significant visits being taken by Western recruits this weekend.

4-star 2028 OT Aden Owolabi visiting Oklahoma

Dru Samia once went from Danville (Calif.) San Ramon Valley to Norman and the Sooners would love to have lightning strike twice with Owolabi, the No. 1 prospect in California in the 2028 class, visiting this weekend when the Sooners host Kentucky. They've been on his extreme short list from the jump and he's well aware of Samia's history with the Sooners, where he was a four-year starter and All-American and Owolabi is even better at the same stage.

4-star 2028 LB Landon Miller visiting UCLA

How much positive momentum has UCLA built with a 5-0 start under Bob Chesney? Miller didn't even have UCLA really on his radar pre-season, and had no plans to take a visit to Pasadena to watch them play. He was at USC two weeks ago, already making one trip to the Southland but then last weekend, took a visit to Oregon and saw the Bruins win in Eugene. That quickly led to the Concord (Calif.) De La Salle linebacker setting up an unofficial visit to UCLA, who never backed down despite having little traction and they're now very much in the race for him.

4-star 2028 QB Titus Huard visiting Kansas State

Kansas State has been in the top echelon of schools for Huard for quite some time. The Highlands Ranch (Colo.) Valor Christian quarterback was in Manhattan last month, but this time, he's bringing the whole family, including his father, Brock, a former NFL quarterback. It's clear that Collin Klein has prioritized Huard, who like Klein, is from Colorado and now getting a second visit, including the family, only enhances their chances with him.

4-star 2028 WR Quincey Clay visiting Oregon

Since Dan Lanning took over at Oregon, the Ducks have had major success in Idaho- Kenyon Sadiq , Gatlin Bair and then last year, Hudson Lewis , have been their success stories. Clay was at the USC-Oregon game in Los Angeles, but instead of USC offering him after the game, the Ducks did instead and now he's planning to visit this weekend for the game with Nebraska and Oregon has been a longtime dream school for him. Like Sadiq, Bair and Lewis, Clay played for RARE 7v7 in Idaho so the Ducks would like to keep that going with the Boise (Idaho) Capital receiver.

4-star 2028 DB Jaelyn Easterling-Flores visiting Oklahoma

Oklahoma already has a commitment from Goodyear (Ariz.) Desert Edge in 2027 cornerback Mikyal Davis . But they'd love to make it consecutive years with Scorpions and they're in the final six for the four-star safety, a Top 100 player nationally and a Navy All-American Bowl selection. The Sooners have been making a big push for him and Davis has been recruiting him to Norman as well and he's another headliner set to visit this weekend.

articles.title: 49ers vs. Commanders Preview: San Francisco Looks to Stay Undefeated
articles.summary: 49ers Aim to Keep Rolling on Monday Night The San Francisco 49ers return home Monday night looking to extend their undefeated start when they host the Washin...
articles.body:
49ers Aim to Keep Rolling on Monday Night

The San Francisco 49ers return home Monday night looking to extend their undefeated start when they host the Washington Commanders at Levi's Stadium. San Francisco enters the Week 6 matchup at 5-0 after an exciting 32-29 road victory over the Seattle Seahawks, while Washington arrives at 1-3-1 following a frustrating 27-27 overtime tie against the New York Giants.

The matchup presents two teams heading in different directions. The 49ers have found ways to win close games, while the Commanders are searching for consistency as they attempt to climb back into the NFC playoff conversation. Kickoff is scheduled for 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN and ABC.

Brock Purdy Leads San Francisco's Offense

Quarterback Brock Purdy has helped guide the 49ers through an impressive opening stretch. Although San Francisco has faced several challenging opponents, the offense has continued producing at important moments.

Purdy threw two touchdown passes against Seattle and helped lead the game-winning drive that set up Eddy Piñeiro's decisive field goal. His ability to distribute the football and make smart decisions has been important to the team's success.

Running back Christian McCaffrey remains another major weapon. His versatility as both a runner and receiver gives head coach Kyle Shanahan several ways to attack opposing defenses. San Francisco will look to establish its running game early, create favorable passing situations and control the tempo.

The 49ers' offense has also benefited from contributions across the roster, allowing the team to remain productive even when individual drives become difficult.

Jayden Daniels Looks to Spark Washington

Washington will rely on quarterback Jayden Daniels to help generate offense against a San Francisco defense that has started the season strongly.

Daniels demonstrated his playmaking ability against the Giants, rushing for 103 yards and two touchdowns while throwing for 199 yards. However, Washington's inability to finish the game left the team with a disappointing tie.

Daniels' mobility could be one of the Commanders' biggest advantages. San Francisco will need disciplined defensive play to prevent him from escaping the pocket and creating explosive gains with his legs.

Washington also needs better protection up front and more consistent execution on third downs. Sustaining drives will be particularly important against a 49ers team that has repeatedly capitalized on scoring opportunities.

The coaching matchup adds another layer to Monday night's game. Shanahan has San Francisco playing confident football, while Quinn needs Washington to respond after letting a potential victory slip away.

For the Commanders, limiting turnovers and improving their second-half execution will be essential. The 49ers, meanwhile, will look to continue their balanced offensive approach and use their home-field advantage.

San Francisco has an opportunity to improve to 6-0 and strengthen its position in the NFC West. Washington needs a complete performance to show it can compete with one of the conference's unbeaten teams.

With Purdy and McCaffrey leading the 49ers against Daniels and Washington's offense, Monday night's matchup offers an important test for both teams as the NFL season moves deeper into October.

articles.title: Tre' Harris to miss Week 6 because of injury
articles.summary: Chargers WR Tre' Harris set to miss at least one game because of his hamstring issue
articles.body:
Los Angeles Chargers WR Tre' Harris (hamstring) did not participate in practice Friday, Oct. 16, and has been ruled out for Week 6.

Why It Matters: Fantasy players can keep an eye on the situation to see how long Harris may be sidelined. Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston will be the main receivers for the Chargers with Harris sidelined. McConkey can be considered a No. 2 fantasy receiver, while Johnston can be a No. 5 receiver.

articles.title: WWE Rumors on Gunther 'Confusion' Backstage, WrestleMania 43 Matches and Stephanie Vaquer's Injury
articles.summary: Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.
articles.body:
Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.

Reported Internal Outlook Regarding Gunther's Booking

Recasting Street Fighter with WWE Stars 🎬

Some in WWE have reportedly been questioning the recent booking direction of two-time world heavyweight champion Gunther.

According to WrestleVotes on Fightful Select (h/t WrestlePurists ), there is "a mild sense of frustration and confusion" over how Gunther has been utilized on SmackDown over the past few weeks.

One source told WrestleVotes that some people in creative have questioned whether The Ring General is being used properly when taking into consideration what he accomplished in 2025 and early in 2026.

On the heels of retiring Goldberg, John Cena and AJ Styles, Gunther heavily pursued the WWE Championship, but he has fallen short in numerous opportunities to win it.

That included a loss to Cody Rhodes at Clash in Italy, and a loss in a Triple Threat match for the WWE title against Rhodes and Sami Zayn at Night of Champions.

Gunther did bounce back to beat SmackDown general manager Nick Aldis at SummerSlam, but he subsequently lost a WWE Championship No. 1 contender's match, and later lost a Money in the Bank ladder match qualifying match.

Amid his recent cold streak, Gunther had been interacting backstage with Danhausen, leading to several instances of The Ring General intimidating him.

Gunther and Danhausen were scheduled to have a match last week, but instead, Gunther decimated Danhausen before the bell even rang.

It has been a strange spot for a serious wrestler like Gunther since Danhausen is one of the preeminent comedic wrestlers in the business.

While it may only prove to be a blip on the radar before Gunther moves on to bigger and better things, Gunther's current position is undoubtedly a bit of a surprise based on how he has been booked and presented for the entirety of his main roster run.

WWE Reportedly Planning Reigns vs. Femi, More for WrestleMania 43

WrestleMania 43 is still about six months away, but WWE reportedly already has a good idea of some of the major matches it wants to headline the show.

According to WrestleVotes on Fightful Select (h/t WrestlePurists ), WWE has discussed Roman Reigns vs. Oba Femi and CM Punk vs. Cody Rhodes for the event. The company reportedly also wants to heavily feature Rhea Ripley provided she is cleared from the knee injury she is currently working her way back from.

WrestleVotes noted that while the aforementioned matches and plans have been proposed and talked about, they are not yet set in stone.

The Reigns vs. Femi idea comes as little surprise, as many have assumed it would be the WrestleMania 43 main event dating back to WrestleMania 42.

Femi beat Brock Lesnar at WrestleMania 42, while Reigns won the World Heavyweight Championship from Punk. After the show, The Ruler called out Reigns.

Oba won King of the Ring and could have challenged Reigns, but he decided to conclude his rivalry with Lesnar first instead, and it was clear at that point that WWE was kicking the proverbial can down the road as it relates to Oba and Roman.

Punk and Rhodes faced off at SummerSlam with Punk beating Rhodes to retain the WWE Championship, but there has yet to be a rematch.

While neither Punk nor Rhodes hold a title right now, it won't be at all surprising if one of them wins back the WWE Championship before WrestleMania 43 to set up another clash between them.

As for Ripley, she has been on the shelf since early June due to a torn meniscus that required surgery.

Assuming Ripley is back in time to build toward a meaningful match at WrestleMania, there is little doubt that she will be put in that spot given her long history of significant WrestleMania matches against the likes of Charlotte Flair, Becky Lynch, Bianca Belair, Iyo Sky and other big names.

The ankle injury Stephanie Vaquer was nursing during Monday night's episode of Raw was reportedly not part of a storyline.

According to Dave Meltzer of the Wrestling Observer Newsletter (h/t WrestlePurists ), Vaquer got legitimately injured at Money in the Bank, although it is not expected to keep her out of action for long.

At Money in the Bank, Vaquer attempted to defend the Women's World Championship against Liv Morgan and Becky Lynch in a Triple Threat match, but Morgan hit her with Oblivion to pin her and win back the women's world title.

On the subsequent episode of Raw, Vaquer was seen backstage on crutches, but she said she would be back in action soon and even teased an eventual singles match against Lynch.

La Primera previously missed an extended period of time when she was injured around the time of WrestleMania 42.

She was off WWE programming for more than three months before returning in August and targeting Morgan, who beat her for the Women's World Championship at WrestleMania.

Vaquer won the title back from Morgan at a live event in her home country of Chile last month, but she dropped it back to Liv about a month later at Money in the Bank.

Now, Vaquer is fighting through another injury, but every indication is that she won't be on the shelf for long this time.

articles.title: Cardinals' rookie RB Jeremiyah Love ruled out vs. Rams with lingering ankle injury
articles.summary: (AP) — Rookie running back Jeremiyah Love won't play for the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday against the Los Angeles Rams because of a lingering left ankle injur...
articles.body:
TEMPE, Ariz. (AP) — Rookie running back Jeremiyah Love won't play for the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday against the Los Angeles Rams because of a lingering left ankle injury.

The No. 3 overall pick out of Notre Dame hasn't practiced all week and was ruled out on the team's injury report released on Friday.

"There's no discussion of IR or anything like that," first-year coach Mike LaFleur said. "We've got to re-evaluate, really every single day. Not good enough obviously right now to go Sunday. It wouldn't be in the best interest of him."

Love has been a big part of the Cardinals' offense through the first five weeks with a team-high 245 yards rushing and a touchdown. He's also caught 11 passes for 36 yards and a TD.

"He's doing good, but you guys see the way he cuts, just being candid, he cuts hard, that's a superpower of his," LaFleur said. "And when he's putting his left foot in the ground, it's just not right right now."

The Cardinals (1-4) enter Sunday's game against the Rams (2-3) on a four-game losing streak and have lost eight straight games against NFC West opponents.

articles.title: John Lynch: George Kittle asked me if we're trying to trade for Khalil Mack
articles.summary: The trade deadline was a topic of conversation for General Manager John Lynch on Friday.
articles.body:
The trade deadline was a topic of conversation for General Manager John Lynch on Friday.

Lynch was a guest on KNBR and he was asked if calls are picking up with the November 10 deadline drawing closer. Lynch said that the calls have picked up of late and that the team has made its own "just to kind of see where the market's at" right now.

Lynch was also asked specifically about interest in Chargers pass rusher Khalil Mack.

"I can't tell you that ," Lynch said, via 49ersWebzone.com. "A lot of people ask me that. We seem to be connected to everyone, and I don't know where that comes from. I had a player ask me that yesterday."

Lynch eventually named tight end George Kittle as the inquisitive player, which isn't surprising "because he asks about everything." Kittle's interest in the prospect makes sense, however. The 49ers are 5-0 and should feel good enough about their chances to make a run that they'd be willing to bolster the roster ahead of the deadline. On the other hand, the Chargers are 0-5 and should be considering picking up assets for the future with this season headed off the rails.

articles.title: Charlotte Hornets jersey history No. 6 Kelly Tripucka 1988-1991
articles.summary: After a trade with the Utah Jazz, former Notre Dame forward Kelly Tripucka spent three seasons with the Charlotte Hornets.
articles.body:
In one of the best trades in Hornets franchise history, Charlotte traded center Mike Brown to the Utah Jazz ahead of the 1988-89 season in exchange for former No. 12 overall pick Kelly Tripucka. After averaging 7.5 points with Utah during the 1987-88 season, Tripucka averaged 22.6 points in his first season with the Hornets, more than a 15-point increase.

The former Notre Dame forward would go on to play three seasons with the Hornets before playing professionally in France. In 227 appearances with Charlotte, Tripucka averaged 14.9 points, 3.4 rebounds, 2.7 assists, 0.9 steals and 0.2 blocks while shooting 45.1% from the field and 35.6% from 3-point range. Throughout his 10-year career between the Hornets, Jazz and Pistons, Tripucka averaged 17.2 points, 3.8 rebounds, three assists and one steal.

articles.title: Meet the team: Macy Comito
articles.summary: After the exodus commenced upon the conclusion of last season, Macy Comito reaffirmed her commitment to Iowa State. Comito originally made her commitment to...
articles.body:
After the exodus commenced upon the conclusion of last season, Macy Comito reaffirmed her commitment to Iowa State.

Comito originally made her commitment to the Cyclones in August of 2024, and officially signed on Nov. 12, 2025. Even if the roster is a little different (nine transfers out and eight coming in is normal, right?) Comito has been in the blueprint for a long time. Bill described her as "born to be a cyclone" as both of her parents attended Iowa State.

Macy Comito has an incredibly decorated resume at the high school level. From Carlisle, Iowa, Comito holds school records in:

Pretty good. She also earned 4A All-State honors three times, First-Team All-Iowa twice, was named All-Conference for all four years of high school, and set a Class 4A record with 42 points in one state tournament game. In the 2025-26 season, she led Carlisle to a state championship victory and was named the 2026 Iowa Class 4A Player of the Year as well as All-Tournament team captain.

Naturally, she also received a 2026 Academic All-State selection and was named to the Academic All-Conference four times, so it is safe to say that she has amassed success both on and off the court.

One of many guards on the new roster, Comito will still have to work to stand out among a roster that is bringing a lot of collegiate experience, albeit primarily from other programs. Still, her quickness, three point prowess, and defensive ability will certainly be utilized throughout the season. A court with Comito, Arriana Jackson, and Evangelia Paulk could be one of the best defensive trios in the Big-12. Iowa State averaged just 5.72 steals per game during conference play last season, which ranked 15th in the conference.

On the offensive side, Bill Fennelly has been outspoken recently about returning to the "Iowa State Way". Any longtime fan reads that and knows that the three pointers are going to be aplenty. "I don't know what the biggest green light there is, but they all have it," Fennelly stated in a recent press conference. That should be music to Comito's ears, as she will have plenty of opportunities to find open teammates beyond the arc as well as finding her own opportunities to pull the trigger from deep. A faster, more dynamic offense may also clear some more driving lanes for the offense, so it will be key to see how Comito maximises the speed and range potential of this offense as one of the point guards.

If you want to buy early in a cyclone of the future, Comito is one of the best bets you can make. Iowa State has been with Comito for her entire life, and if she can translate the success that she experienced at Carlisle over to the collegiate level? You better watch out.

articles.title: Washington Football Second-Year WR Beacon of Light on Bleak Offense
articles.summary: Despite not producing as many touchdowns as Washington has needed through the first half of 2026, Dezmen Roebuck has been the go-to guy so far.
articles.body:
Washington Huskies second-year wide receiver Dezmen Roebuck has statistically been one of the best in the country through the first half of the 2026 college football season.

The 5-foot-11, 190-pound pass catcher is No. 6 in the FBS with 286 yards after catch and No. 5 in receptions (43) going into the Huskies ' second Big Ten road game this Friday at Purdue. Although the Marana, Arizona native has just 387 receiving yards, tied for No. 59 in the country and just seven more yards than his classmate and teammate Chris Lawson, there is more to Roebuck than that.

"It's Dez," wide receivers coach Kevin Cummings responded Tuesday when asked about the most physical run blocker in his room. "Yeah, it's Dez. It was fun watching him the other night he had a battle with Iowa's nickel (Jacob Wallace). They were getting after it. That was fun to watch."

Roebuck was one of three receivers to haul in a touchdown from backup quarterback Elijah Brown in the Huskies' 41-24 loss to the Hawkeyes at Husky Stadium last Friday. Late in the third quarter, the UW slot receiver broke free just enough from fifth-year Iowa defensive back Deshaun Lee to cut the deficit to 34-18 following a two-point conversion.

Through his first six games as a freshman in 2025, Roebuck had nearly the same receiving yards (318) and an equal number of touchdowns (2). However, as expected with the departures of veterans Denzel Boston and Omari Evans, Roebuck has more than doubled his receptions total from 18 to 43, and that held true when Brown came in for the injured Demond Williams Jr. in the second half.

Jedd Fisch and the Huskies' offense will need Roebuck to continue to produce as the unit searching for a significant improvement against the Boilermakers. Through three conference games against Illinois, Minnesota and UCLA, fourth-year coach Barry Odom's Purdue defense has only had one opposing receiver compile a 100-yard receiving game, Illini veteran Collin Dixon, who put up 10 receptions for 118 yards and a touchdown in a 24-17 loss two weeks ago.

Roebuck doesn't need to have his first 100-yard game in conference play—he's the only UW receiver to have a 100-yard game this season (121 yards vs Eastern Washington), with second-year tight end Baron Naone (103 yards) being the other, also against the Eagles—for the Huskies to return from West Lafayette with the first victory in league play.

He does, however, need to continue to produce as he has for Fisch and the offense to have at least a chance to overcome the Boilermakers at Ross–Ade Stadium.

The final weeks of the 2026 North Carolina high school football regular season are upon us as Week 9 kicks off Friday, Oct. 16.

Every Wilmington-area team except North Brunswick will suit up Friday, with several big matchups in the Port City as all four Wilmington schools face fellow city opponents.

Laney (3-4, 2-1 Carolina Coast) hosts Hoggard (6-1, 3-0) in a matchup the Bucs haven't won since 2010. Across town, Ashley (4-3, 2-1) hosts New Hanover (2-5, 1-2) in a rivalry that has been revived in recent years. Find full schedules for every Wilmington-area high school football team here .

articles.body:
Photos of Yorktown's and Delaware County's tributes to the late Chris Wilson Jr.

The final week of the IHSAA football regular season is upon us.

This week, The Star Press will have extended coverage of the Muncie Central Bearcats (6-2) as they host Class 5A No. 7 Lafayette Jefferson (6-2). Both teams are 4-0 in North Central Conference play with wins over Anderson, Kokomo, Marion and Richmond, setting up a matchup for the NCC championship in the regular season finale. The Bronchos have won the NCC each of the last three seasons, while the Bearcats have not won the conference since 2004. Last year's season finale presented a similar situation, and while Central was able to keep things close in the first half, Jefferson eventually pulled away for a 55-22 victory.

Elsewhere in East Central Indiana, Wes-Del (7-0) will look to finish off an undefeated regular season as it hosts Cambridge City Lincoln (0-8). Shenandoah (1-7) is also at home to host New Castle (2-6) in an Eastern Crossroads Conference matchup and the first-ever meeting on the gridiron between the two Henry County rivals. Other teams at home this week include Blackford (1-7) hosting Madison-Grant (6-2) in a Central Indiana Conference game, Winchester (4-4) hosting Union City (2-6) in a key Tri-Eastern Conference rivalry, and Yorktown (5-3) hosting Mt. Vernon (Fortville) (4-4) in a Hoosier Heritage Conference game.

Meanwhile, Delta (4-4) will play its final HHC game at Class 5A No. 4 New Palestine (5-3), while Jay County (3-5) will pay a visit to Heritage (5-3) in an Allen County Athletic Conference game. The only other East Central Indiana team on the road this week is Monroe Central (3-3), who will travel to Knightstown (6-2).
